# Nomana-IT Documentation

> Documentation of the software published by Nomana-IT, a software publisher and JD Edwards / Oracle / AI consultancy. Liberty Next is a low-code application platform; Nomaflow (scheduling and orchestration), Nomasx-1 (security, licence compliance and segregation of duties) and Nomajde (JD Edwards EnterpriseOne companion) are built with and for Liberty Next. NomaUBL is a standalone e-invoicing platform for the French reform (UBL, Plateforme Agréée, e-reporting). The site also documents open-source JD Edwards and BI Publisher APIs. Liberty Next and NomaUBL include built-in AI assistants, powered by Claude (Anthropic), that answer from the documentation and from the data of the instance.

Company: https://nomana-it.fr/ · AI services: https://nomana-it.fr/ai/ · Full text: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/llms-full.txt · French: https://docs.nomana-it.fr/llms.fr.txt

## Products — overviews and getting started

- [Liberty Next — Getting Started](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/getting-started/): Liberty Next — connector-driven low-code framework. Configuration drives discovery: define a SQL or API connector in TOML, expose its queries to a screen or a dashboard, and the React UI builds the grid, the form and the filters automatically.
- [Why Liberty Framework](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/overview/): Liberty Framework is a low-code platform for building internal applications — admin tools, BI dashboards, integration glue, customer portals — without writing a frontend. Define data sources and screens in the Settings UI; the framework renders the grid, the edit dialog, the dashboard, the assistant.
- [Liberty Next — What you can build](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/what-you-can-build/): What teams build with Liberty Next — admin apps over existing tables, dashboards, an interface over an ERP database, integration and data-loading jobs, workflows with conditional forms — with what the framework provides, what is left to configure, and when another tool fits better.
- [What is Nomaflow](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/overview/): Nomaflow is the job scheduler built into Liberty Next: cron-scheduled jobs made of steps (SQL, file loads, Python, HTTP, LDAP, other jobs), retries, a run history with logs, missed-schedule detection and notifications — no separate worker or broker.
- [Nomaflow — Getting started](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/getting-started/): A first Nomaflow job in a few minutes: open the Jobs page, create a job, add a sql_query step, set a schedule, run it by hand and read the run.
- [Nomasx-1 — The compliance and licence-optimisation platform](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/overview/): Nomasx-1 unifies enterprise security, Object Usage Tracking, Oracle and JD Edwards licence compliance and Segregation of Duties into one platform — source-agnostic, audit-ready, on-premise.
- [Nomajde — The JD Edwards companion application](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/overview/): Nomajde sits next to JD Edwards EnterpriseOne and turns the day-to-day work — master data, security, reporting, monitoring — into one set of grids with inline edits. SQL and AIS API combined, no fat-client navigation, no manual exports.
- [NomaUBL — The unified e-invoicing platform](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/getting-started/): NomaUBL bridges any ERP to the French e-invoicing reform — UBL generation, pre-submission validation, Plateforme-Agréée routing, lifecycle tracking and operations on a single platform. Source-agnostic, PA-agnostic, ready for the 2026 RFE.
- [Open source API for JD Edwards and BI Publisher](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/getting-started/): Open source API for JD Edwards and BI Publisher

## AI assistants

- [Liberty Next — AI assistant](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/ai-assistant/): The Liberty Next AI assistant: the drawer opened from the AI Assistant button, what it can do (read the connectors' queries, call API endpoints, propose configuration, read allowed web pages), how it is restricted (ai:chat, allowed connectors, read-only queries, data scope), and its settings.
- [Liberty Next — Expose data to the AI assistant](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/expose-to-ai/): Recipe — choose what the AI assistant reaches and help it pick the right query: the ai:chat permission, the allowed connectors, read queries only, the user's data scope, and query labels and descriptions written for the model.
- [NomaUBL — AI Capabilities](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/ai-capabilities/): The NomaUBL AI assistant — a chat panel that knows the page and the invoice you are on, answers from the NomaUBL documentation, from the generated documentation of the instance and from its data (invoice dossier, period figures, backlog, lifecycle, validation errors, server log, integrity checks, e-directory), follows diagnostic playbooks, proposes follow-ups, and only reads.

## Liberty Next — framework

- [Liberty Next — First app walkthrough](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/getting-started/first-app/): Build a working Liberty Next app end to end: a pool, a SQL connector with its queries generated from a table, a screen with a grid and an edit dialog, and a menu entry — all from Settings, applied without a restart.
- [Liberty Next — Project layout](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/getting-started/project-layout/): File map of the two repositories — liberty-next (framework binary) and liberty-apps (per-installation configuration). What lives where, what is committed, what is per-installation, and how LIBERTY_APPS_DIR routes the framework to the apps repo.
- [Liberty Next — Installation — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/overview/): How to install Liberty Next: pick Docker (light or full layout) or a Python install, run one command, sign in, add the licence and the licensed apps, switch on HTTPS. Every step afterwards — status, backup, upgrade, rollback — goes through the same command.
- [Liberty Next — Architecture](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/architecture/): What a Liberty Next install is made of, whatever the way it is installed (Docker light, Docker full, Python with systemd): one server process, a framework database, configuration files, the optional licensed-apps bundle and two secrets — where each one lives, how the server starts, how its health is checked.
- [Liberty Next — Docker](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/docker/): Install Liberty Next with Docker: prerequisites, the light layout (one container, SQLite) and the full layout (PostgreSQL, Traefik, pgAdmin, Portainer), install options, image tags, the recorded compose files, Docker Swarm.
- [Liberty Next — Python server](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/python-server/): Install Liberty Next without Docker: pipx install from PyPI, secrets in an environment file, PostgreSQL bootstrap with liberty-admin init-db, the licensed apps, a systemd unit, and liberty-ops for status, backups and upgrades.
- [Liberty Next — Licensed apps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/deploy-prebuilt-apps/): Install Nomasx-1 and Nomajde on Liberty Next: the licence key, the apps wheel, the application databases created by the installation jobs, the per-entity merge that keeps your changes on every upgrade, and the first connection to the source system.
- [Liberty Next — HTTPS and Traefik](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/traefik/): Switch Liberty Next to HTTPS on the full Docker layout: a Let's Encrypt certificate or your own, switching mode or back to HTTP with ./liberty ssl, the Traefik dashboard password, and what to forward when you use your own reverse proxy.
- [Liberty Next — Bundled visual tools](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/portainer/): How to use the Portainer and pgAdmin instances that ship with the Liberty Full Docker layout — first-run setup, common operator tasks, Docker socket security trade-offs, Swarm specifics.
- [Liberty Next — Operations](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/operations/): Run a Liberty Next install day to day: ./liberty status and doctor, start, stop and logs, backups and restores, common administrator tasks, the liberty-ops twin for Python installs, and the usual problems with their fix.
- [Liberty Next — Upgrade and rollback](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/upgrading/): Upgrade Liberty Next with one command: ./liberty upgrade (Docker) or liberty-ops upgrade (Python) checks the install, takes a backup, installs the new release and the apps, applies the schema migrations and records a report; rollback undoes it. Swarm upgrades and versioning.
- [Liberty Next — Production checklist](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/installation/production/): What to check before a Liberty Next server goes into production: pinned release, HTTPS, passwords, secrets kept off the server, exposed ports, sign-in protection, backups, logs, monitoring — and what the shipped Docker layouts already harden for you.
- [Liberty Next — Step 1 — Set up the CRM project](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/setup/): Start the Build-a-CRM tutorial: the tables for customers, deals and activities, sample data, and the crm connector that will become the app. End state: the framework running, a superuser signed in, the tables ready.
- [Liberty Next — Step 2 — The Customers screen](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/customers/): Build the first screen of the CRM: the customers queries generated by the CRUD wizard, audit columns stamped by the server, a screen with a grid and an edit dialog, and the app's menu that turns the crm connector into an app.
- [Liberty Next — Step 3 — Deals and relationships](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/deals/): Second CRM screen: the dictionary gives labels and lists of values (an enum for the customer status, lookups for the customer and the stage of a deal), the Deals screen links each deal to its customer, and the deal's activities appear in a tab of its dialog.
- [Liberty Next — Step 4 — Sales pipeline dashboard](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/dashboard/): Add a pipeline dashboard to the CRM: aggregate queries, KPIs compared with the previous period, a saved bar chart of the pipeline by stage, a table of recent activities, and the menu entry that opens it.
- [Liberty Next — Step 5 — Roles and sign-in](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/auth/): Decide who sees what in the CRM: a read-only role and a sales role built on the app's menu tree, writes granted beyond the menus, two test users, a data scope by country from a user attribute, and sign-in with the company's identity provider.
- [Liberty Next — Step 6 — AI assistant and a daily job](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/tutorial-crm/ai-and-jobs/): Finish the CRM: the AI assistant answers questions over the CRM's queries within each user's rights, and a Nomaflow job flags stalled deals every morning and notifies the sales team.
- [Liberty Next — Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/connectors/): A connector is how Liberty Next reaches a data source: a SQL connector holds the named queries of a database pool, an API connector the named endpoints of a web API. Edited in Settings → Connectors; a connector with a menu is an app.
- [Liberty Next — Queries — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/overview/): How Liberty's Connectors page is organised — Settings / Tables / Queries / Sequences / Lookups — and the four kinds of queries it holds.
- [Liberty Next — Create from a database table](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/create-from-database/): The CRUD Wizard — point Liberty at an existing table, tick the columns, get the four CRUD queries auto-generated and saved in one click.
- [Liberty Next — Create a custom query](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/create-custom/): Write a standalone query by hand — the Queries view, the editor form, the writable switch, the params block, the SQL editor with autocompletion and tokens.
- [Liberty Next — Clone a query or a connector](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/clone/): Duplicate one query inside a connector, duplicate every CRUD query of a table, or clone a whole application (connector + dictionary + screens + menu + dashboards + charts).
- [Liberty Next — Sequences and lookups](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/sequences-and-lookups/): The Scaffold modal — tick a table and a column, get a generated sequence (next id) or lookup (value + label) query plus the matching dictionary entry, saved in one click.
- [Liberty Next — Parameter binding](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/parameter-binding/): How a query's :name parameters get their values — declared defaults on the query, param_binds on the caller (fixed value, another field, #LOGIN_USER# / #SYSDATE# built-ins), and {{LOGIN}} / {{SYSDATE}} tokens resolved by the server.
- [Liberty Next — Per-dialect SQL variants](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/queries/per-dialect-sql/): Ship one Liberty query with different SQL on Postgres, Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite and DB2 — the per-dialect `sql` map, when to use it, common gotchas.
- [Liberty Next — Dictionary](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/dictionary/): The dictionary defines each data item once — label, format, rule, default, translations — and every query column that references it inherits that definition. Entries, enums, lookups, sequences and framework enums, shared or per connector, edited from Settings → Dictionary.
- [Liberty Next — Screen Creation Assistant](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screen-assistant/): A guided wizard that turns a set of database tables — or an existing connector query — into a working screen, dialog and menu item in one pass. Pick the source, choose the grid columns (default shared view), optionally lay dialog columns into tabs, review the dictionary, place a menu entry, create.
- [Liberty Next — Screens — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/overview/): The Screens page — left scope bar of apps, flat list of screens, click to open the Screen Designer's 9 tabs (General / Queries / Columns / Views / Summary / Dialog / Actions / Row menu / Export).
- [Liberty Next — Create a screen from a query](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/create-from-query/): Wire a `_get` query to a fresh screen — the General tab and the Queries tab walked through field by field; the grid appears, edits land via the write queries.
- [Liberty Next — Columns](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/columns/): The Columns tab — set each column's display title, format, dictionary reference, edit rule, default and filtering once; both the grid and the dialog use them.
- [Liberty Next — Dialog builder](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/dialog-builder/): The Visual Builder — a three-column Figma-style canvas (Palette / Canvas / Inspector) where you drag fields onto tabs, set properties, wire lookups and add per-tab actions.
- [Liberty Next — Conditional fields](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/conditional-fields/): Make a dialog field appear, become required, lock itself or take a forced value only when another field has a given value — set on the column from the screen editor's inspector, with worked examples.
- [Liberty Next — Form conditions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/form-conditions/): Every conditional setting of a screen column — show, require, lock, force a default, change the rule or skip the write depending on another field's value — and the screen's row-level editable_when rule. One condition shape: a field and a value, ANDed.
- [Liberty Next — Actions and lifecycle](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/actions-and-lifecycle/): The Actions tab — dialog hooks (on_load / on_save / on_cancel), toolbar buttons, row hooks (on_insert / on_update / on_delete / on_duplicate), the row menu, the action types with their param_binds, prompts, chains and shared actions.
- [Liberty Next — Nested tabs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/screens/nested-tabs/): Embed a child-record form (nested_form) or a related-rows grid (nested_table) in a dialog tab — same dialog, multiple data sources.
- [Liberty Next — Saved grid views](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/saved-views/): Save a data grid's columns, sort, filters and grouping as a named view — your own views follow you across devices, and an admin can publish shared views with one set as the default. Also covers the screen's Summary view — parent rows counted by the database, detail rows loaded on demand — and day-grain filtering on timestamp columns.
- [Liberty Next — Apps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/apps/overview/): What an app is in Liberty Next — a connector with a menu, shown in the app picker — what belongs to it (queries, dictionary scope, screens, menu, charts), how users switch between apps, and how an app is copied, moved between environments or installed ready-made.
- [Liberty Next — Menus — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/overview/): The Menus page, the flat-items-linked-by-parent model, the five leaf kinds (screen / query / endpoint / dashboard / page), and how a menu plus show_in_switcher turns a connector into an app.
- [Liberty Next — Make a connector an app](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/make-connector-an-app/): A connector becomes an 'app' visible in the application picker when it has a menu attached and show_in_switcher is on. Plus how the optional home field decides the landing page.
- [Liberty Next — Build the tree](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/build-the-tree/): The tree editor — add folders and items, drag to reorder, indent/outdent to reparent, clone, rename, find usages. Every action's exact button and behaviour.
- [Liberty Next — Item types](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/item-types/): The five leaf kinds — screen / query / endpoint / dashboard / page — what each opens, the target field's shape, the connector rule, and when to reach for each.
- [Liberty Next — Permissions and roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/permissions-and-roles/): The roles filter on a menu item, the underlying sql / api permission inherited from the target, how empty folders collapse, and how the menu prunes per user.
- [Liberty Next — Translations and icons](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/menus/translations-and-icons/): Menu labels per language with the l map (l.fr, l.de…), how the language is chosen, and the icon names the Liberty Next sidebar can draw.
- [Liberty Next — i18n](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/apps/i18n/): Languages in Liberty Next — the interface in English and French, the per-language labels (l) of dictionary entries, enum values, menu items, dialog tabs and prompts, and how the language of each request is chosen.
- [Liberty Next — Dashboards](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/dashboards/): Liberty Next dashboards: KPIs, charts and tables over connector queries on a 12-column grid, a period with presets and comparison with the previous period, dictionary filters, a cache with Refresh — built in Settings → Dashboards and opened from the menu.
- [Liberty Next — Charts](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/charts/): A saved chart draws the result of a connector query as bars, lines, areas or a pie: an X column, one or more series with their colour and axis, and an aggregation. Built in Settings → Charts or saved from a screen's Chart view, then reused in dashboards.
- [Liberty Next — Data Explorer](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/overview/): The Liberty Next Data Explorer: free analysis of an app's data without writing SQL — fields pane, rows, measures and filters, a period, table, pivot, charts and KPI views, detail rows and drill, calculated fields, saved analyses, dashboards and Excel / PDF export, over a model built in Settings → Explorer.
- [Liberty Next — Build a model](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/model/): Settings → Explorer in Liberty Next: an explorer model per data mart — the hub, the entities (a query with its cardinality, key, measures, hidden columns and default date), the relations on column pairs, and a model filled from a Screen Assistant preset.
- [Liberty Next — Analyse data](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/analysis/): Using the Liberty Next Data Explorer: the fields pane, the Rows, Measures and Filters shelves, the period, Top N, the table, pivot, bar, line, pie and KPI views, the detail view, the drill to the rows behind a figure and the record dialog.
- [Liberty Next — Calculated fields](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/calculated-fields/): Calculated fields in the Liberty Next Data Explorer: the editor (name, label, expression, field and function pickers, Test), the expression language — arithmetic, comparisons, conditions, in, is empty, date, text and number functions — and how the result type makes a measure or a dimension.
- [Liberty Next — Saved analyses and dashboards](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/explorer/saved-and-dashboards/): Keeping Data Explorer work in Liberty Next: saved analyses, private or shared, with an audience; dashboards of saved analyses with their own period and layout; Excel and PDF export; the analyses and dashboards an app ships.
- [Liberty Next — Secure — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/overview/): The security of a Liberty Next install: who can sign in (local users, OpenID Connect, sign-in throttle), what they can open (roles, allow and deny permissions), which rows they see (data scope), how secrets are stored (ENC: values), and the licence.
- [Liberty Next — Sign-in — local and OIDC](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/sign-in/): Local users, optional OIDC sign-in against any compliant provider (Keycloak, Azure AD, Auth0, Okta…). What the user sees at sign-in.
- [Liberty Next — Roles and permissions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/roles-and-permissions/): Liberty Next roles: what a role grants, edited on the application's own menu tree (inherit / allow / deny per folder or entry, sidebar preview), the rules beyond the menus, and the data scope that restricts which rows a role sees — by company, by any dictionary item, from a user attribute.
- [Liberty Next — Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/users/): The Settings → Access → Users tab — add local users, manage OIDC users that landed at first sign-in, assign roles, toggle is_active and is_superuser, reset passwords.
- [Liberty Next — Encrypted secrets](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/encrypted-secrets/): How Liberty Next stores pool passwords, API credentials, the licence key, the AI key, the OIDC client secret and the SMTP password: encrypted as ENC: values on every save from Settings, with the install's master key.
- [Liberty Next — License key](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/secure/license-key/): The Liberty Next licence key: what it unlocks (Nomasx-1, Nomajde), where to paste it (Settings → App → License), how to check it (liberty-license, /api/license), what happens without it, and how to replace it before it expires.
- [Liberty Next — App settings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/settings-app/): Settings → App in Liberty Next: the six sections — App (name, address, logs, language, UI defaults, hot reload, Oracle thick mode), License, AI Assistant, Notifications (email), OpenID Connect (SSO), PDF branding — what each field does, which secrets are encrypted, and what needs a restart.
- [Liberty Next — Settings UI](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/settings-ui/): The Liberty Next Settings page: one editor per configuration file, grouped per connector (connectors, dictionary, actions, menus, screens, charts, dashboards, reports, notifications) or shared (pools, theme, access, app, history, release notes), how a save is validated and applied, and Reload config.
- [Liberty Next — Environment variables](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/environment-variables/): The environment variables Liberty Next reads — secrets, configuration folders, database bootstrap, container behaviour, operations — the ${VARIABLE} references allowed in every TOML file, and the variables of the Docker .env file.
- [Liberty Next — Hot reload](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/hot-reload/): How Liberty Next applies configuration changes without a restart: Reload config (POST /admin/reload), the file watcher of [app] hot_reload and what it reloads per file, pools, Settings → App, and what still needs a restart.
- [Liberty Next — Encryption & secrets](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/encryption-secrets/): How Liberty Next keeps secrets out of its configuration files in clear: ENC: values encrypted with the master key, secret fields encrypted on every save from Settings, ${VARIABLE} references, liberty-crypto, and what to do with the master key.
- [Liberty Next — Config history & versioning](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/configuration/config-history/): Every config save is snapshotted, every screen save captures its dependency closure as a restorable bundle, version changes are logged, and the bundled release notes are readable in-app — all under Settings → History.
- [Liberty Next — Packages](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/packages/): Ship configuration from one Liberty install to another. the Nomaflow Package page: pick a few screens / menu items / dashboards as seeds, the dependency walker pulls in everything they reach (queries, dictionary, charts), and the package exports as a ZIP. On the target install, upload + pick a merge strategy (merge / overwrite / replace all). Same UI handles both sides.
- [Liberty Next — Plugins — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/overview/): A plugin is a Python package on disk that Liberty makes importable at startup. It carries custom callables your Nomaflow python steps reference — the escape hatch for anything declarative steps can't express.
- [Liberty Next — Plugins](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/apps/plugins/): Custom Python code called by Liberty Next — where plugin packages live, how a Nomaflow python step and a screen's call_plugin action call a module:function, what the framework injects (connectors, ctx, settings, changesets), how to query connectors and what to return.
- [Liberty Next — Write a callable](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/write-a-callable/): The function contract for a python step's callable — signature, auto-injected kwargs (connectors / ctx / settings), return-value normalisation, sync vs async, error and cancellation semantics.
- [Liberty Next — ETL primitives](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/etl-primitives/): The liberty.etl toolkit — six async helpers your plugin callables compose into ETL flows: copy_query_to_table, snapshot_rows, delete_rows, truncate_table, insert_audit_record, run_query.
- [Liberty Next — Deploy and debug](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/build/plugins/deploy-and-debug/): The apps repo layout, LIBERTY_APPS_DIR, the dev shell with uvicorn --reload, the production deploy pattern, log lines you'll grep for, and the testing setup.
- [Liberty Next — CRUD over an existing table](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/crud-existing-table/): Recipe — put a list / add / edit / delete interface on an existing database table from Settings: pool, queries generated by the CRUD wizard, screen, menu entry.
- [Liberty Next — Excel export](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/excel-export/): Recipe — export a screen to Excel: the grid's Export menu (current view, Excel or CSV, visible or all columns), and configured workbooks from the screen's Export tab — several sheets, one file per group, built on the server.
- [Liberty Next — Files and attachments](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/file-upload/): Recipe — what Liberty Next offers for files: screens have no attachment field, but a row can carry the address of a document stored elsewhere, a file's rows can be imported into a screen, and a Nomaflow job can load a file chosen at run time.
- [Liberty Next — Audit trail](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/audit-trail/): Recipe — record who created and last changed each row, and keep the history of every write, without trusting the browser: {{LOGIN}} / {{SYSTIMESTAMP}} tokens in the write queries, dictionary rules, and the screen's audit table.
- [Liberty Next — Bulk import](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/bulk-import/): Recipe — load many rows from an Excel or CSV file: the screen's Import dialog, which checks every row against the screen's rules and the database before saving the valid ones, and the Nomaflow file_load step for recurring loads.
- [Liberty Next — Multi-step form / workflow](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/multi-step-form/): Recipe — an approval workflow on a status column: one guarded query per transition, row-menu actions with confirmation and a prompt for the reason, permissions per transition, fields shown or locked by status, read-only closed rows, notifications and a daily reminder job.
- [Liberty Next — OIDC sign-in](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/oidc-sso/): Recipe — let users sign in with the company's identity provider (Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta, Auth0…): register the application at the provider, fill Settings → App → OpenID Connect (SSO), then give the new users their roles.
- [Liberty Next — Scheduled report email](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/scheduled-report-email/): Recipe — a report e-mailed on a schedule: a Nomaflow job that computes the figures, a notification rule on the job's success that e-mails them, and the dashboard or screen where readers find the detail. What to do when an attached file is required.
- [Liberty Next — Row-level access](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/framework/cookbook/row-level-access/): Recipe — limit the rows each user sees in Liberty Next: by company, region or any dictionary item with a role's data scope and a user attribute; or to the rows a user owns with the {{USER}} token in the query.
- [Liberty Next — Monitoring — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/monitoring/overview/): How to watch a running Liberty Next server: the Monitoring page for superusers (sessions, record locks, database pools, runtime, live log), the health endpoints for probes, and the command-line status and doctor.
- [Liberty Next — The Monitoring page](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/monitoring/dashboard/): Block by block, the Liberty Next Monitoring page: the four KPIs, database pools, runtime, connected users, record locks and the live log tail — what each value means and when to act.
- [Liberty Next — Health endpoints](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/monitoring/health-endpoints/): Liberty Next health endpoints: /health (liveness), /ready (readiness — the framework database answers) and /info (version and counts, more details when signed in), with examples for Docker, Kubernetes and external probes.
- [Liberty Next — CLI reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/references/cli/): Every Liberty Next command-line tool: liberty-admin (database bootstrap, users, roles, data scope, install jobs, schema migrations), liberty-ops and ./liberty (operations), liberty-connectors (run a query without the web app), liberty-crypto (ENC: values), liberty-license (check the key).
- [Liberty Next — REST API reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/references/rest-api/): A map of the Liberty Next REST API by domain — health, sign-in, connectors and data, screens, dashboards, menus, reports, notifications, saved views, Nomaflow jobs, change packages, access and configuration — with the access rule of each family. The exact request and response shapes are in the built-in OpenAPI pages.

## Nomaflow — scheduling and orchestration

- [Nomaflow — Concepts](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/concepts/): The Nomaflow vocabulary: job, step, schedule, preset, trigger, run, parameters, retry policy, log level, alerts — what each one is and where it is set.
- [Nomaflow — Catalogue — the Jobs page](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/catalog/): The Nomaflow Jobs page: the toolbar, the retention and missed-schedule panels, what a job card shows, switching a job on or off, Run now and Run with parameters (presets, steps, file uploads, log level), Cancel, Clone, Delete and Export.
- [Nomaflow — Create a job](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/create/): The Nomaflow job editor: the Job section (id, schedule, timezone, tags, enabled), presets and their schedules, the retry policy, alerts, shared parameters and the step pipeline — and what is set only in jobs.toml.
- [Nomaflow — Schedules](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/jobs/schedules/): When Nomaflow jobs run: the five-field cron syntax and its day-of-week numbering, timezones, the preview of the next runs, the Schedule view, schedulable presets, and missed schedules recorded as MISSED runs.
- [Nomaflow — Steps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/steps/): The seven Nomaflow step types — sql_query, sql_copy, file_load, python, http, ldap_sync, call_job — what each one does, its fields and defaults, and what it records in the run.
- [Nomaflow — Run history](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/runs/history/): Where Nomaflow runs are recorded and how to read one: the run states, the Run detail page (summary, per-fire overrides, steps, log with Follow and Download), the Job Runs list, and how long the history is kept.
- [Nomaflow — Troubleshoot](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/runs/troubleshoot/): Fixing Nomaflow runs: a run that failed, a step that does the wrong thing, a run that hangs, a cancel that does not stop a Python step, a schedule that does not fire, a job missing from the list, an empty log.
- [Nomaflow — Scheduled sync](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/scheduled-sync/): Recipe — copy tables every night from an operational database to a reporting database with sql_copy, refresh the aggregates with sql_query, and be warned when it fails or does not run.
- [Nomaflow — API pull](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/api-pull/): Recipe — fetch records from a REST API every hour with a Python step and write them through a connector's query, with the token kept out of the job.
- [Nomaflow — Conditional cleanup](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/workflows/conditional-cleanup/): Recipe — purge old rows every night, but only when there are enough of them, in batches, with the decision and the counts in the run log.
- [Nomaflow — Bundled jobs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/bundled-jobs/): The Nomaflow job catalogue shipped with the liberty-apps wheel — install / preload / refresh / sync / SOD / audit jobs that drive Nomasx-1 and Nomajde without the operator writing a single line of TOML. Run from Nomaflow → Catalogue → ▶ Run now, schedule via the standard scheduler, or trigger from CI.
- [Nomaflow — Change packages](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/change-packages/): Capture every tracked data write into a reviewable package — old → new diffs grouped by entity, exclude entries cherry-pick style, submit / approve / reject the package, export a JSON bundle and apply it on another environment with full pre-image drift detection. The canonical use case is promoting JD Edwards security from dev to prod.
- [Nomaflow — Custom Python steps](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/custom-python/): Write a Python function for a Nomaflow python step: where it lives, what it receives (its arguments, connectors, the run context), what it returns, how it logs to the run, how it fails and how it is cancelled.
- [Nomaflow — Notifications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/notifications/): Liberty Next notifications: rules that react to a screen write, a Nomaflow job event (failure, success, cancel, missed schedule, long run) or a screen action, and deliver to the in-app bell, by e-mail or through a connector query or endpoint. SMTP account, recipients, placeholders, job alerts.
- [Nomaflow — Administration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomaflow/administration/): Running Nomaflow on a server: where runs and files are kept, one instance, what happens on restart, run history retention, the run log buffer, who can use the Jobs pages, backup and health.

## Nomasx-1 — security and licence compliance

- [Nomasx-1 — Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/users/): List of users known to Nomasx-1 across every connected application — identifier, name, account status, creation date, last login, last usage, last update.
- [Nomasx-1 — Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/roles/): Catalog of all roles defined in each connected application — application, role identifier, role name, sequence.
- [Nomasx-1 — Assignments](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/assignments/): Active role assignments — which user holds which role, on which application, with effective and expiration dates.
- [Nomasx-1 — Roles not used](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/roles-not-used/): Roles defined in the source system but not assigned to any user — the candidates for cleanup.
- [Nomasx-1 — Users without roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/users-without-roles/): Active users with no role assignment on a connected application — the orphan accounts to investigate.
- [Nomasx-1 — Roles matrix](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/roles-matrix/): Distinct role combinations held by users on each connected application, with the number of users behind each combination.
- [Nomasx-1 — Duplicate users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/duplicate-users/): Users with several accounts pointing to the same person (Address Number / Employee ID), grouped by application.
- [Nomasx-1 — Users Audit](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/users-audit/): Per-user audit view — identity, organisation, country and last usage by module — for a deep dive on a single account.
- [Nomasx-1 — LDAP Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/users/): Raw LDAP / Active Directory user catalog fed into Nomasx-1 — Active Directory attributes side-by-side.
- [Nomasx-1 — Users without AD](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/users-without-ad/): Users known to a connected application but absent from the corporate LDAP / Active Directory — technical accounts, ghosts, or unsynced identities.
- [Nomasx-1 — Users by applications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/users-by-applications/): Cross-tab of LDAP departments and applications, with each user's source-system account and roles — the source view for the per-department Excel export.
- [Nomasx-1 — LDAP Settings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/security/ldap/settings/): Groups AD departments and drives the per-department Excel export of the Users by applications view.
- [Nomasx-1 — Menus](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/menus/): Application menu tree, level by level, with the JDE objects each leaf launches and the licence component they belong to.
- [Nomasx-1 — Rights — Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users/): Object-level rights granted directly to a user — what each user can run, change, add or delete in the source system.
- [Nomasx-1 — Rights — Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/roles/): Object-level rights granted at the role level — the backbone of the security model.
- [Nomasx-1 — Rights — Users / Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users-roles/): Object-level rights pivoted by (user, role) — what each user can run, both directly and through every role they hold.
- [Nomasx-1 — Rights — Users / Menus](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users-menus/): Rights joined to the menu tree — what each user can reach, with the menu path leading to each object.
- [Nomasx-1 — Rights — Roles / Menus](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/roles-menus/): Role-level rights joined to the menu tree — what each role grants in terms of navigation, by licence component.
- [Nomasx-1 — Rights — Users / Roles / OUT](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/rights/users-roles-out/): Effective rights union of the declared rights matrix and the objects users actually invoked, as captured by Object Usage Tracking.
- [Nomasx-1 — Conflicts — Summary](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/summary/): Headline view of segregation-of-duties conflicts — number of users in conflict, broken down by business process and risk.
- [Nomasx-1 — Conflicts — Details](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/details/): Line-by-line backing data for every segregation-of-duties conflict — user, both incompatible activities, the objects and the two source roles.
- [Nomasx-1 — Conflicts — Proven](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/proven/): Segregation-of-duties conflicts confirmed by activity log evidence — the user holds the rights AND has actually exercised them on both sides.
- [Nomasx-1 — Conflicts — Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/users/): Distinct users in conflict on a connected application — the headline list of accounts to remediate.
- [Nomasx-1 — Conflicts — Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/conflicts/roles/): Distinct pairs of roles that produce a segregation-of-duties conflict — the role couples to redesign.
- [Nomasx-1 — Activity log](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/activity-log/): Database-level activity log — every transaction recorded by user on tables of the connected application.
- [Nomasx-1 — OUT — Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/components/): Object Usage Tracking summary by licence component — how many users used each component and when it was last touched.
- [Nomasx-1 — OUT — Details](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/details/): Object Usage Tracking detail — every (user, object) pair captured by the source system, with last-used date and version.
- [Nomasx-1 — OUT — Users / Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/users-roles/): Object Usage Tracking with the user's status, type and link — the per-user view of which licence components they actually consume.
- [Nomasx-1 — OUT — Objects](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/applications/out/objects/): Object Usage Tracking grouped by object — which programs of a licence component have ever been invoked.
- [Nomasx-1 — Oracle](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/database/oracle/): Oracle database properties read from each connected application — product, version, CPU, named-users counts, options and storage.
- [Nomasx-1 — Audit Trail](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/database/audit-trail/): Header of the database-level audit trail — one row per audited operation, grouped by application, date, schema and table. Each row expands to a field-level BEFORE / AFTER diff parsed on demand from the stored DML statement, plus purge and rebuild-values jobs to manage the history.
- [Nomasx-1 — Audit Lookup](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/database/audit-lookup/): Detailed audit lookup — for each audited mutation, the before / after value of every changed column.
- [Nomasx-1 — CSI](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/csi/): Customer Support Identifier — list of the Oracle support contracts the connected applications are entitled to.
- [Nomasx-1 — JD Edwards](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/jd-edwards/): JD Edwards licence overview — active users, transactional users, dormant accounts and orphan transactional accounts per JDE application.
- [Nomasx-1 — Oracle](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/oracle/): Per-database list of Oracle licence options with a required / not required indicator — the inventory to compare with the licences actually subscribed.
- [Nomasx-1 — Subscribed Licenses](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/subscribed/): Subscribed licences inventory — quantities of each component covered by each CSI contract, grouped by metric and price list.
- [Nomasx-1 — Usage Report](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/usage-report/): Per-application × per-component compliance — observed user counts versus subscribed quantity, with the compliance delta.
- [Nomasx-1 — Financial Report](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/licenses/financial-report/): Financial impact of the non-compliant rows — additional licence cost and three years of support per application × component.
- [Nomasx-1 — JD Edwards Licence Audit](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/reports/audit-licences/): A one-click compliance and optimisation audit for a JD Edwards application — licence inventory, real usage, financial exposure and a remediation plan, rendered as a PDF or Markdown deliverable. Bilingual (French default, English available); the report opens on a headline KPI band and inline charts (active-users donut, components-by-usage bar, financial risk by component).
- [Nomasx-1 — Security & SoD Assessment](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/reports/security-sox/): A one-click security-posture and segregation-of-duties review for a connected application — user lifecycle, privileged access, role and object-security hygiene, SoD conflicts and a remediation plan, rendered as a PDF or Markdown deliverable.
- [Nomasx-1 — Applications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/global/applications/): Registry of every connected application — identifier, type, database, host and credentials Nomasx-1 uses to reach the source system.
- [Nomasx-1 — Custom Queries](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/global/custom-queries/): User-defined SQL fragments overriding the default Nomasx-1 queries on a per-application basis.
- [Nomasx-1 — SoD — Process](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/process/): Catalog of business processes that group the activities monitored by the segregation-of-duties matrix.
- [Nomasx-1 — SoD — Activities](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/activities/): Named activities within each business process — the atomic units the segregation-of-duties matrix combines.
- [Nomasx-1 — SoD — Risks](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/risks/): Named risks within each business process, with the severity level used to weight the segregation-of-duties findings.
- [Nomasx-1 — SoD — Matrix](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/matrix/): Pairs of incompatible activities — the SoD matrix that defines which activity combinations trigger which risk.
- [Nomasx-1 — SoD — Objects](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/sod/objects/): Source-system programs attached to each SoD activity — the technical objects whose execution counts as performing the activity.
- [Nomasx-1 — Users properties](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/security/users-properties/): Per-user flags — technical, generic, linked, privileged — that drive licence calculations and audit filtering.
- [Nomasx-1 — Department](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/security/department/): Standalone catalog of AD department / group pairs — the source of values offered as drop-downs across the LDAP screens.
- [Nomasx-1 — System Code](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/system-code/): Mapping of every JDE System Code to its functional module and to the licence component it falls under.
- [Nomasx-1 — Reclassification](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/reclassification/): Override of the JDE object → SY mapping when the default classification is wrong or missing.
- [Nomasx-1 — Prerequisite](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/prerequisite/): Inter-component prerequisites — when buying component X requires having component Y.
- [Nomasx-1 — Restrictions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/jde/restrictions/): Mutually-exclusive components — when buying component X excludes the right to use component Y.
- [Nomasx-1 — Oracle Versions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/oracle/versions/): Catalog of Oracle database versions recognised by Nomasx-1 and their licence component.
- [Nomasx-1 — Oracle Options](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/oracle/options/): Catalog of Oracle database options recognised by Nomasx-1 and the licence component each one falls under.
- [Nomasx-1 — Oracle Features](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/oracle/features/): Catalog of Oracle database features Nomasx-1 tracks, each linked to a licence component.
- [Nomasx-1 — Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/pricing/components/): Master catalog of licence components — price list, category, friendly name.
- [Nomasx-1 — Metrics](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/pricing/metrics/): Catalog of licensing metrics — Application User, Named User Plus, Processor, Employee, etc.
- [Nomasx-1 — Pricing](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/settings/pricing/pricing/): Unit list price and support fee per component × metric — the price book the financial report uses to compute the cost of non-compliance.
- [Nomasx-1 — global-settings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomasx1/admin/global-settings/): Click on add or edit to set a new datasource or modify an existing datasource and follow the wizard

## Nomajde — JD Edwards companion

- [Nomajde — UDC Types](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/master-data/udc-types/): User Defined Code Types — the catalogue of UDC groups defined in JD Edwards, with inline edit and create from a single grid.
- [Nomajde — UDC Codes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/master-data/udc-codes/): User Defined Codes — the individual values inside each UDC type, with inline grid editing for bulk maintenance.
- [Nomajde — User Management](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/user-management/): Add, edit and provision JD Edwards users from a single grid — SQL writes the user master and display preferences, AIS REST provisions the security record and the password.
- [Nomajde — Role Management](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/role-management/): Maintain JD Edwards users and roles in one place — descriptions, attached roles, environments, and the security workbench import workflow.
- [Nomajde — Role Relationships](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/role-relationships/): Maintain the JD Edwards role-inheritance graph in a single grid — pair source and target roles, set effective and expiration dates, bulk-upload from Excel.
- [Nomajde — Environments](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/environments/): Maintain the JD Edwards environment list per user and per role — production, test, development, conference room, with the order in which they appear at sign-on.
- [Nomajde — Security Workbench](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/nomajde/security-maintenance/security-workbench/): Maintain every JD Edwards security entry — application, action, row, column, processing-option, tab, exit, image — on a single grid with inline edit.

## NomaUBL — e-invoicing

- [NomaUBL — Installation — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/overview/): Stand up a NomaUBL server — JDK 17 + an Oracle or PostgreSQL database + the JAR. Runs as a long-lived Java process, one per environment, started through the nomaubl.sh wrapper. Optional systemd unit and reverse proxy for production.
- [NomaUBL — Requirements](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/requirements/): What the host needs before installing NomaUBL — JDK 17, an Oracle or PostgreSQL database, OS support matrix, ports, file-system permissions and the optional reverse-proxy / TLS layer.
- [NomaUBL — Install and layout](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/install-and-layout/): Run -install (directly via java -jar, or via the nomaubl.sh / nomaubl.cmd wrapper) to provision an environment. Understand the directory layout produced — config / input / process / ubl / template / shared resources — and how to install several environments side by side on Linux, macOS or Windows.
- [NomaUBL — Configure](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/configure/): After the install, every connector, scheduler interval and operational setting is configured from the Settings UI — not by hand-editing config files. Start the service, sign in, then walk through the Configuration section.
- [NomaUBL — Service supervision](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/service-and-systemd/): Run NomaUBL as a long-lived service on Linux/macOS or Windows — nomaubl.sh or nomaubl.cmd for start/stop/status, a systemd unit (Linux) or NSSM Windows service (Windows) for auto-restart on boot, and an optional nginx reverse proxy in front for TLS and a friendly hostname.
- [NomaUBL — Upgrade](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/upgrade/): Move an installed NomaUBL environment forward to a new release. One command — nomaubl.sh upgrade on Linux/macOS or nomaubl.cmd upgrade on Windows — handles the JAR swap, schema migrations, reference-data merge, customer XSL merge and service restart. Writes a full report and keeps a rollback backup.
- [NomaUBL — Demo Corpus](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/demo-corpus/): Fill a NomaUBL demonstration instance with fictitious but realistic data — issued invoices and credit notes from UBL files, JDE-like spools and text PDFs, supplier invoices, lifecycles, e-reporting envelopes and notifications — through the real pipelines, from Settings › Global or the command line, and reset it in one step.
- [NomaUBL — Desktop app](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/installation/desktop-app/): Install NomaUBL as a desktop application on Windows and macOS from Chrome, Edge or Safari: its own window and icon, no browser bars, one app per environment named after it, always the server's version; HTTPS required.
- [NomaUBL — Monitoring — overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/monitoring/overview/): Where to look when running NomaUBL in production — the in-app IT dashboard, the Processing Log, the service log file, the build-info / license endpoints. Plus the patterns to wire external monitoring.
- [NomaUBL — Service and logs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/monitoring/service-and-logs/): Operate NomaUBL from the host — wrapper status (nomaubl.sh on Linux/macOS, nomaubl.cmd on Windows), the log file for live diagnostics, /api/build-info and /api/license for machine-readable checks. Patterns for external alerting and log forwarding.
- [NomaUBL — Billing overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/billing-overview/): The NomaUBL Billing overview, the landing page: the invoices of the period in amounts (revenue and VAT net of credit notes, invoice count, transmission or acceptance rate) compared with the previous period, twelve months of invoiced amounts, what needs a decision in amounts, and the split per company, per transaction type and the e-reporting position, for sales or purchases.
- [NomaUBL — Operations](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/dashboard/): The NomaUBL Operations dashboard: what the team has to handle on the period, as three work queues (in progress, to correct and send again for IT, a new invoice to issue for customer service), the activity chart, the invoices blocked the longest, the latest events, the top failing rules, the PA round-trip time and the e-reporting coverage, for sales or purchases.
- [NomaUBL — IT dashboard](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/tech-dashboard/): The NomaUBL IT dashboard: a health strip (application, database, disk, memory, scheduler, configuration), the four action cards (send failed, waiting for review, to reprocess, to reprocess in full), processing over the last 14 days (volume, errors, retries, time per document), what is running right now, recent errors, and folded technical details (system, filesystem, JVM, configuration check, database tables, links).
- [NomaUBL — Statistics](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/statistics/): The NomaUBL Statistics dashboard: where the invoices of the period stand in five stages, how they flowed over the period, how long the open ones have waited, the statuses and most frequent reasons, splits per transaction type and activity code, and a detail table by activity, status and reason, all compared with the previous period, with Excel and PDF exports.
- [NomaUBL — E-Invoicing](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/invoices/): The day-to-day NomaUBL invoice list — search, filter and inspect every invoice; open a detail view to consult parties, lines, VAT, lifecycle and PDF; edit, copy, resend or e-mail invoices; manually set a status.
- [NomaUBL — E-Documents](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/edocuments/): Browse every document captured in the NomaUBL archive — not only those that became invoices — with the archived source spool and the generated UBL side by side, and query the same archive over REST.
- [NomaUBL — E-Reporting](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/ereporting/): E-reporting declarations to the Plateforme Agréée — generate French flux 10.1 (B2C invoice detail) and flux 10.3 (B2BINT aggregated) for a chosen company, type and period; track each report's lifecycle, resend on demand, download the submitted XML.
- [NomaUBL — E-Directory](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/edirectory/): Look up a French company in the INSEE registry by name, SIREN or SIRET, then check whether each match is reachable on the PPF directory for e-invoice delivery.
- [NomaUBL — VAT Declaration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/vat-declaration/): Aggregate every invoice for a period on the standard French CA3 form rows — sales / purchases × domestic / intra-EU / outside-EU × VAT rate × invoice type — with drill-down to the individual invoices behind each figure, and one-click Excel and CA3-formatted PDF exports.
- [NomaUBL — Reports](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/overview/): Reporting for NomaUBL — four cards: SQL integrity checks against a source system, and the audit, implementation and technical reports generated as PDF or Markdown. Status statistics are on the Statistics dashboard, free analyses in the Explorer.
- [NomaUBL — Audit Report](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/audit-report/): Audit the electronic invoicing of a period from the NomaUBL tables — executive summary compared with the previous period, volumes, situation by status, backlog, lifecycle and delays, errors and their handling, operations and consistency checks — as a PDF or Markdown file, in French or English.
- [NomaUBL — Implementation Report](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/implementation-report/): Generate the technical and functional documentation of a NomaUBL instance from its configuration and database — context, architecture, built-in rules, documents, UBL transform and mappings, platform settings, operations, security and reference data — as a PDF or Markdown file, in French or English, with secrets masked.
- [NomaUBL — Technical Report](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/reports/technical-report/): The NomaUBL technical report — the developer documentation of the release generated from the code scans bundled at build: architecture, data model, flows, configuration reference, status model, impact matrix, API reference, command line, build and packaging, as PDF or Markdown, in French or English.
- [NomaUBL — Explorer](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/explorer/): The NomaUBL Explorer — build your own analyses of the invoice data without SQL: fields of seven entities on Rows, Measures and Filters shelves, table, pivot, detail and charts, calculated fields, drill-down to the invoices, dashboards, ready-made analyses for IT, accounting and audit, exports to Excel, PDF and PNG, daily digests.
- [NomaUBL — Notifications](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/notifications/): Portal inbox for status-change alerts emitted by NomaUBL — All / Unread tabs, mark-all-read, per-row dismiss, click-through to the linked invoice. Combined with the navbar bell that polls every 30 s and previews the last six entries, the page is the read-side of the notification system.
- [NomaUBL — Diagnostics](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/diagnostics/overview/): The NomaUBL Diagnostics page gathers errors and logs in four views of one page — Integration errors, Processing log, Failures and Server log — each granted separately per role, with dashboard links landing on the right view.
- [NomaUBL — Integration Errors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/diagnostics/integration-errors/): Failure-analysis tool over the validation table — by-rule cards ranking the top failing rules, a by-event flat table for row-level investigation, and a detailed view that groups events by invoice. Each rule code is decorated with the human description extracted from the bundled Schematron files. Filter by category (UBL / Integration), severity, document key; the Unmatched only checkbox keeps the original orphan-error view one click away. The detailed view exports every event in scope, even collapsed ones.
- [NomaUBL — Processing Log](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/diagnostics/processing-log/): Browse the NomaUBL runtime log — every START / END / intermediate event recorded during XML, UBL, BIP and FTP processing. Group events by job to see status and duration at a glance, or switch to the flat event stream for forensic analysis.
- [NomaUBL — Failures](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/diagnostics/failures/): The Failures view of NomaUBL Diagnostics lists every failure with one shape — validation findings, PA rejections, send and import failures, processing failures per file, failed job runs — unresolved only by default, with server-side search and links to the invoice, the processing log or the scheduled jobs.
- [NomaUBL — Server Log](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/application/diagnostics/server-log/): The Server Log page shows the end of the NomaUBL server log file, newest lines first, with severity and module filters, a text search and auto-refresh — no shell access needed.
- [NomaUBL — Fetch Input](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/fetch-input/): Batch-automated equivalent of Extract and Process — scan a directory or the BIP Print Queue, pick items in a checkbox list, and run the same Extract → Process pipeline on every selected item.
- [NomaUBL — Import](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/import/): Confirm that invoices submitted to the Plateforme Agréée have actually been imported — async import polling that updates each pending 9906 invoice to 10 (Deposited) or 9907 (PA rejected the import).
- [NomaUBL — Retrieve Statuses](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/retrieve-statuses/): Pull lifecycle status events from the Plateforme Agréée — XP Z12-012 codes 200, 201, 206, 207, 210, 213… — and apply them to the local lifecycle table and the invoice header. Watermark-based incremental retrieval.
- [NomaUBL — Scheduled Jobs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/scheduled-jobs/overview/): One NomaUBL page for every job the server runs on a schedule — PA import poll and status retrieval, e-reporting cycle, received invoices, batch document jobs, daily digests, auto-retries, lifecycle checks and the retention purge — with trigger, state, last and next run, Run now, Pause / Resume, run history and an in-place editor.
- [NomaUBL — Daily Digest](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/scheduled-jobs/daily-digest/): Scheduled jobs → Digest schedules a recurring email of the day's integration errors, with the full event list attached as an Excel file. Multiple digests can be configured per recipient subset, each with its own send time, lookback window, severity filter and per-column routing — different teams receive different cuts of the same data.
- [NomaUBL — Auto-Retry](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/scheduled-jobs/auto-retry/): Scheduled jobs → Auto-retry schedules a daily sweep that replays every invoice in a chosen technical-error status (default 9904 at 3 a.m.) back to the Plateforme Agréée. Multi-status picker, optional lookback window, per-row throttle, shared with the Send Failed card on the IT dashboard. The overnight pickup for batches stuck on the PA side.
- [NomaUBL — Lifecycle Checks](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/sync/scheduled-jobs/lifecycle-checks/): Schedule the NomaUBL lifecycle integrity check (backfill PA statuses the poll missed) and the ordering check (re-sequence events recorded out of order) to run daily without an operator — the same repairs as the Retrieve Statuses page buttons, plus the matching CLI modes for cron.
- [NomaUBL — Process Document](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/processing/document/): Single processing entry point for one or many invoice files. The pipeline is selected automatically by the document's source property — XML spool (XSL → UBL) or already-formed UBL 2.1 — so the same form covers both flows.
- [NomaUBL — Extract and Process](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/processing/extract-and-process/): Chain an extraction (Archive / FTP / BIP) and a processing run (XML or UBL) in a single click — equivalent to running an Extract page then the matching Processing page back-to-back.
- [NomaUBL — Process API](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/processing/process-api/): Execute an API connector endpoint defined in Configuration → API Connectors — pick a connector and an endpoint, override parameters at runtime, inspect the HTTP response and any extracted value.
- [NomaUBL — Validate](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/validate/): Validate a UBL document against XSD schema and Schematron business rules — straight UBL or upstream XML transformed to UBL via a template's XSL pipeline.
- [NomaUBL — XSL Editor](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/xsl-editor/): Map source XML spool fields to UBL 2.1 business terms (BT codes) through a visual form — no hand-written XSLT required. AI-assisted auto-mapping included.
- [NomaUBL — Rule Sets](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/rule-sets/): NomaUBL rule sets — EN 16931 basic, EN 16931 and France extended (CTC): which UBL fields a standard requires, which validation packs apply, how a document chooses its set, and how the XSL editor's mapping tab, the invoice window and the reference pages read it.
- [NomaUBL — Post-Transform](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/post-transform/): NomaUBL post-transform — convert the validated UBL into another syntax (CII D16B with the shipped ubl-to-cii.xsl, a national format with your own stylesheet) while UBL stays the pivot: output next to the UBL, download from the invoice window, sending through the platform connector.
- [NomaUBL — XML Viewer](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/xml-viewer/): Open any XML file — local or server-side — in a Monaco editor with syntax highlighting, pretty-print, line numbers and save-to-server. The lightweight companion to the validator and the XSL Editor.
- [NomaUBL — Overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/overview/): How NomaUBL's UBL Defaults work — a base defaults file (ubl-defaults.xsl) plus optional per-template override layers, resolved field group by field group at generation time.
- [NomaUBL — UBL Header Defaults](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/ubl-header-defaults/): UBL Defaults — Header tab. UBL version, customization ID (BT-24), default country (BT-40 / BT-55) and per-template date input format.
- [NomaUBL — Scheme IDs](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/scheme-ids/): UBL Defaults — Scheme IDs tab. ISO 6523 / UNTDID 1153 / EAS scheme identifiers attached to SIREN, SIRET, GLN, electronic endpoint and delivery location.
- [NomaUBL — Invoice Type](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/invoice-type/): UBL Defaults — Invoice Type tab. Default UBL invoice type code (BT-3) and rule-based selection driven by source XML conditions.
- [NomaUBL — Business Process Type](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/business-process-type/): UBL Defaults — Business Process Type tab. French Cadre de facturation (BT-23) — invoice nature (goods / services / mixed) and lifecycle stage (deposit / already paid / final / subcontracting / multi-vendor / e-reporting).
- [NomaUBL — Payment Code Mapping](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/payment-code-mapping/): UBL Defaults — Payment tab. Default payment means code (BT-81) and source → UBL code mapping based on UNCL 4461.
- [NomaUBL — Unit of Measure Mapping](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/unit-of-measure-mapping/): UBL Defaults — Units tab. Default unit code (BT-130) and source → UN/ECE Recommendation 20 unit code mapping.
- [NomaUBL — Currency Code Mapping](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/currency-code-mapping/): UBL Defaults — Currency tab. Default currency (BT-5) and source → ISO 4217 currency code mapping.
- [NomaUBL — Document Type (BAR Routing)](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/document-type-bar-routing/): UBL Defaults — Document Type tab. BAR routing classification (B2B / B2G / B2BINT / B2C / OUTOFSCOPE / ARCHIVEONLY / DOCUMENT) used to dispatch the document inside the Plateforme Agréée.
- [NomaUBL — VAT Categories](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/vat-categories/): UBL Defaults — VAT tab. Default VAT category, zero rate, source → UBL category mapping (BT-118 / BT-151) and category → VATEX exemption-code mapping (BT-121).
- [NomaUBL — Country & Classification](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/country-classification/): UBL Defaults — Country & Classification tab. Sets the source-side format for the line country of origin (BT-159) and the fallback classification code, scheme listID and version (BT-158).
- [NomaUBL — Allowances / Charges](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/allowances-charges/): UBL Defaults — Allowances / Charges tab. Sets the fallback reason text and reason code per direction (BR-42 for allowances, BR-43 for charges); the ChargeIndicator picks the pair at emit time.
- [NomaUBL — Suppliers / Companies](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/suppliers-companies/): UBL Defaults — Suppliers tab. Directory of seller (AccountingSupplierParty) records used as defaults when the source XML omits them, keyed by company code.
- [NomaUBL — French Legal Notes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/ubl-tools/ubl-defaults/french-legal-notes/): UBL Defaults — Notes tab. Document-level legal notes (BT-22) carrying mandatory French wording — payment delay, recovery fee, general terms — with note-type prefix.
- [NomaUBL — Extract Archive](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/extract/extract-archive/): Extract an archived invoice document from the NomaUBL database back to disk — original source XML (F564230) or generated UBL 2.1 (F564231) — by document key (FEDOC / FEDCT / FEKCO).
- [NomaUBL — Extract FTP](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/extract/extract-ftp/): Browse a remote SFTP server and download a file to a local directory on the NomaUBL server — uses the SFTP credentials configured in FTP Connectors.
- [NomaUBL — Extract BIP](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/extract/extract-bip/): Extract a BIP (BI Publisher) job's payload from the JD Edwards Print Queue — input XML (F95630) or rendered output (F95631) or both — to a directory on the NomaUBL server.
- [NomaUBL — Documents](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/documents/): Configure how each document type is parsed from a source XML spool, read from a UBL invoice, or pulled live from a SQL query / REST API, then transformed for processing and rendered as PDF.
- [NomaUBL — PDF Templates](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/pdf-templates/): First-class library of reusable PDF layouts. Each template is a pdf-template resource referenced by documents by name. Edit once, propagate everywhere via a full-screen visual builder — palette of sections on the left, live preview in the centre, inspector with options + custom-block tree editor on the right.
- [NomaUBL — Action Bindings](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/actions/): Bind the regulatory seller actions surfaced in the invoice detail modal — Payment Received, Credit Note, Corrected Invoice, Send Completed, Cancel Accounting, New Invoice, Resend to PA — to one or more API or SQL connector calls. Per-binding multi-call list with Stop on failure flag, response chaining via {call.N.fieldName}, and a Scope selector that lets each company override the default e-invoicing template.
- [NomaUBL — Notification Rules](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/notification-rules/): Define which invoice status changes generate a notification, what they say, who receives them and through which channels (portal inbox, email, external API call). Each rule is a notification-rule resource saved in config-notifications.json; a synchronous Test panel lets you fire a rule end-to-end before flipping it on for production.
- [NomaUBL — Watched Folders](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/watched-folders/): Watched folders pick up JD Edwards PDF / XML outputs from mounted directories, convert PDFs to XML in parallel, and run one batch per document — scheduled as a batch job on the Scheduled jobs page, on demand from the page, or from the command line.
- [NomaUBL — File Versions](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/file-versions/): Browse the NomaUBL environment file tree, view and restore previous versions, edit text files in-app, view PDFs, and export / import multi-file packages between environments.
- [NomaUBL — Promotion](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/promotion/): Move NomaUBL configuration between instances item by item — document templates with their XSL, RTF and Schematron files, PDF templates, lists, notification rules, digests, auto-retries, lifecycle checks, connectors and settings templates — in a package whose instance keys never travel, with a preview, a field diff and a version snapshot before every write.
- [NomaUBL — Command Line](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/management/command-line/): NomaUBL command-line interface — service control via nomaubl.sh, direct modes of the JAR (install, serve, xml, ubl, fetch-import, fetch-status, fetch-single, fetch-all, extract) with every argument and flag explained.
- [NomaUBL — Settings Overview](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/settings-overview/): How the NomaUBL Settings page is organised — a navigation by intent (Platform, Security, E-invoicing, E-reporting, Jobs & inbound, Views & UI, API, SQL and FTP connectors, Reference data, Custom data), a search over every field label, hint and key, Advanced folds for rarely used settings, and the header actions.
- [NomaUBL — E-Directory](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/edirectory/): Configure the connection to the French PPF (Portail Public de Facturation) directory and the INSEE company search used to validate addressing codes and look up customer information before sending an e-invoice. Two-tab layout: Directory (Enable Check + INSEE Search) and Connector (api-connector picker + per-task endpoint overrides).
- [NomaUBL — E-Invoicing](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/einvoicing/): Configure how NomaUBL talks to a Plateforme Agréée (PA) — through a reusable api-connector reference, an optional SFTP fallback for outbound submission, and a status-retrieval section. Four-tab layout: UBL Validation · PA Connection · FTP/SFTP · Status. The api-connector holds the auth flow and endpoints; this page only references it by name and overrides per-task endpoint names when needed.
- [NomaUBL — E-Reporting](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/ereporting/): Configure how NomaUBL produces and submits e-Reporting bundles — Sender / Issuer identity, schedule, the api-connector that holds the PA's HTTP transport, and the SFTP fallback for outbound submission. Four-tab layout: Identity · Reporting · PA Connection · FTP/SFTP. paMode = API / FTP / empty replaces the legacy sendToPA Y/N flag.
- [NomaUBL — Fetch Invoices](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/fetch-invoices/): Configure which JD Edwards BI Publisher (BIP) jobs NomaUBL retrieves for batch processing, and which document to use for each.
- [NomaUBL — Integrity Reports](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/integrity-reports/): Integrity reports are read-only SQL checks that list what is missing or wrong in NomaUBL compared with a source system — print jobs never integrated, amounts that differ — shown on Reports → Integrity, with an optional action on the selected rows.
- [NomaUBL — Global](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/global/): Application-wide NomaUBL settings in ten tabs: directories and environment, processing, server log, PDF rendering, email, AI assistant, job defaults (quiet window, bulk send, retention, BIP watermarks), license, authentication and default periods.
- [NomaUBL — OIDC](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/oidc/): Configure single sign-on for NomaUBL: OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE flow, IdP issuer / client / scopes, claim mapping keyed by email, allowed email domains, Google Workspace hd claim enforcement, auto-provisioning with a default role. Drives the login screen jointly with the Auth Mode field on the Global template.
- [NomaUBL — Document Types](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/document-types/): Configure the seven NomaUBL document type codes that anchor the French e-invoicing / e-reporting reform: per-type description, default selection, send-to-PA policy, output mode and file-retention flags.
- [NomaUBL — Statuses](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/system/statuses/): Define the invoice lifecycle statuses NomaUBL recognises: regulatory code, internal Tag, bilingual labels, the event name expected by the Plateforme Agréée, the Collect flag for PA polling, and the Groups that drive the dashboard counters and SQL filters. Search box, expandable per-status form, multi-select groups with coloured chips.
