- [NomaUBL — Reference Lists](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/reference-lists/): Catalogue of the standard French e-invoicing reference lists embedded in NomaUBL: ISO/UN/CEN code lists, Factur-X / EN 16931 business term values, and PA-side action and rejection codes.
- [NomaUBL — Custom Lists](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/custom-lists/): Create operator-defined reference lists (code / FR / EN labels) and assign them to grid columns so dropdowns and filters render automatically. Each list can be edited row by row or synced from an API / SQL connector.
- [NomaUBL — List Views](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/list-views/): Edit the per-view column spec (labels, format, alignment, width, filter allow-list) for every NomaUBL list page — Invoices, Integration Errors, Processing Log, E-Reporting — and add new columns from the view's column catalog without writing code.
- [NomaUBL — Period picker, navigation and lists](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/default-periods/): The NomaUBL period picker shared by the dashboards and lists — ten presets, a two-month calendar, the date basis of each page, the Exclude reviewed errors switch — and the Default periods settings that choose the period each page opens on, for every view or view by view.
- [NomaUBL — API Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/api-connectors/): Define generic REST API connectors used by NomaUBL to talk to a Plateforme Agréée, a source ERP (JD Edwards AIS, SAP, NetSuite, custom) or any HTTP service: connection, authentication, endpoints catalogue, and built-in test runner.
- [NomaUBL — SQL Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/sql-connectors/): Define generic SQL connectors used by NomaUBL to read or write rows on any reachable database — Oracle or PostgreSQL — through named parameterised queries. Each query carries a name, label, description, parameter spec, the SQL itself with :param placeholders, and a Writable flag. The editor has Connection / Queries / Test tabs and the runtime binds parameters through PreparedStatement so values are never string-substituted into SQL.
- [NomaUBL Database](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/database-connectors/nomaubl/): Configure the connection to the NomaUBL application database (Oracle or PostgreSQL): JDBC URL, credentials, schema, the full table catalogue (invoice, e-reporting, auth, notifications), the Columns mapping editor, a Validate Schema panel that compares the bundled DDL to the live schema, and a one-click Initialize action.
- [NomaUBL — JD Edwards](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/database-connectors/jdedwards/): Configure the access to the JD Edwards database NomaUBL reads from when extracting BIP outputs: JDBC URL, credentials, schema, BIP table names and post-extraction record handling.
- [NomaUBL — FTP Connectors](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/ftp-connectors/): Configure SFTP access to the JD Edwards Enterprise Server so NomaUBL can pull spool files directly from the JDE PrintQueue.
- [NomaUBL — Users](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/security/users/): Manage NomaUBL user accounts: create, edit, deactivate or delete users, assign them a role and reset their password.
- [NomaUBL — Roles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/configuration/security/roles/): Manage NomaUBL roles: row-based grants stored in F564254 across four tabs — Access (pages + features), Actions (per-action whitelist), Data scope (companies + row filters), Members. Card list with copy / delete, friendly page labels from the sidebar i18n, granular per-button action grants and column-based row filters that gate the list views, the per-row endpoints and the rendered PDF stream.
- [NomaUBL — Status Reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/status-reference/): Invoice life-cycle statuses for the French e-invoicing reform — codes 200 to 501 (XP Z12-012) with actor, phase, mandatory/factoring tags and allowed actions.
- [NomaUBL — Reason Codes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/reason-codes/): Reason codes attached to invoice life-cycle statuses for the French e-invoicing reform — refusal (B2B), PA rejection and irregularity codes from XP Z12-012 Annex A.
- [NomaUBL — UBL Reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/ubl-reference/): UBL field reference for the French e-invoicing reform — 455 UBL terms from the AFNOR XP Z12-012 V1.4 matrix, each with its XPath, cardinality, profile, data type, code list, definition, usage note and the business rules that constrain it, grouped by section.
- [NomaUBL — Business Rules](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/business-rules/): The French CTC business rules of the AFNOR XP Z12-012 V1.4 matrix — twelve points of attention written from chapter 4.4 of the standard, and the full rule catalogue (BR-FR controls, consistency, flux 1/10.1 mapping, numeric formats, multi-seller, PPF) with the terms each rule constrains.
- [NomaUBL — Schematrons](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/schematrons/): The NomaUBL Schematrons page: read the rules of each Schematron pack the validator runs — EN 16931, CIUS-FR, extended CTC FR, Chorus Pro, NomaUBL, e-reporting, and the customer packs named by the document templates — one row per rule with severity, description and context, and the test and message of each rule.
- [NomaUBL — Database Tables](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/database-tables/): NomaUBL database schema reference — every table that backs the application: invoice archive, UBL header / lines / VAT, lifecycle events, validation errors, processing log, e-reporting, notifications and authentication. Functional descriptions, primary keys and field references for Oracle and PostgreSQL.
- [NomaUBL — Developer Reference](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/references/developer/): The NomaUBL Developer page — tables and columns, configuration keys, flows, impact analysis and the API of the instance — generated at build time from the database DDL, the configuration classes, the settings editors, the Java sources and the OpenAPI document.
- [NomaUBL — Release Notes](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/nomaubl/release-notes/): NomaUBL release notes — every user-visible change shipped in the platform, version by version, in reverse chronological order. Mirrors the in-app Release Notes page.

## JD Edwards and BI Publisher APIs

- [JDEBIP - Export XML source or PDF Output from JD Edwards BLOB fields](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/jde-api/jdebip/): This class can be used to export blob column for BI Publisher from JD Edwards Database. This class can be extended to export BLOB for all tables
- [JDEBSN - Export source code for BSFN from JD Edwards BLOB field (F98780R)](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/jde-api/jdebsfn/): This class can be used to export blob column for BSFN from JD Edwards Database. This class can be extended to export BLOB for all tables
- [NOMABC - Barcode 128 for BI Publisher](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/bip-api/nomabc/): Simple java class to encode string and display barcode 128 with BI Publisher RTF template
- [NOMABIP - Java package with Oracle BI Publisher API](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/api/bip-api/nomabip/): API to integrate easily JDEdwards and BI Publisher regardless of JDEdwards Tools Release

## Liberty Core — React UI components and services

- [Liberty Core — BarChart Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/charts/bar/): The `BarChart` component is a customizable bar chart using Chart.js.
- [Liberty Core — LineChart Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/charts/line/): The `LineChart` component provides a customizable line chart using Chart.js.
- [Liberty Core — PieChart Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/charts/pie/): The `PieChart` component provides a customizable Doughnut/Pie Chart using Chart.js.
- [Liberty Core — ConfirmationDialog Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/dialogs-overlays/confirmation/): The `ConfirmationDialog` component provides a standard confirmation popup with customizable actions.
- [Liberty Core — Dialog Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/dialogs-overlays/dialog/): The `Dialog` component is a modal dialog that appears over the main content.
- [Liberty Core — Dialog Export Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/dialogs-overlays/export/): The `DialogExport` component provides a modal dialog to select export options before exporting data.
- [Liberty Core — Popper Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/dialogs-overlays/popper/): The `Popper` component provides a floating UI container that appears next to an anchor element.
- [Liberty Core — Tabs Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/dialogs-overlays/tabs/): The `Tabs` and `Tab` components allow navigation between different views or settings.
- [Liberty Core — FormsTable Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/forms-components/advanced-grid/): The `FormsTable` component is a fully featured table system designed for complex enterprise applications.
- [Liberty Core — Dashboard Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/forms-components/dashboard/): The Dashboard Configuration defines the structure and content of dashboards within the Liberty Core framework.
- [Liberty Core — InputCheckbox Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/inputs-forms/checkbox/): The `InputCheckbox` component is a reusable checkbox input with built-in state management.
- [Liberty Core — InputColor Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/inputs-forms/color-picker/): The `InputColor` component allows users to select colors using an interactive color picker.
- [Liberty Core — DatePicker Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/inputs-forms/date-picker/): The `DatePicker` component is a styled date selection field that allows users to pick a date from a calendar popup.
- [Liberty Core — InputEnum Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/inputs-forms/enum/): The `InputEnum` component is an advanced dropdown that retrieves values dynamically from an enumeration source.
- [Liberty Core — InputFile Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/inputs-forms/file-upload/): The `InputFile` component allows users to upload files via a button-based interface.
- [Liberty Core — Input Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/inputs-forms/input/): The `Input` component is a reusable text input field supporting: - Multiple variants: `outlined`, `filled`, and `standard` - Error handling and helper text - Start and end adornments - Multiline text area support - Clear button…
- [Liberty Core — Select Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/inputs-forms/select/): The `Select` component provides a dropdown for selecting options, with support for filtering, free text input, and clearing the selected value.
- [Liberty Core — AppsContent Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/main-components/content/): The `AppsContent` component is the core layout container for Liberty Core applications.
- [Liberty Core — AppsHeader Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/main-components/header/): The `AppsHeader` component provides a standard header with multiple actions such as: - Opening a menu drawer - Toggling dark mode - Opening user settings - Opening chat - Signing out
- [Liberty Core — AppsLogin Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/main-components/login/): The `AppsLogin` component provides the authentication interface for Liberty Core applications.
- [Liberty Core — AppsMenus Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/main-components/menus/): The AppsMenus component provides a dynamic, customizable menu system for Liberty Core applications.
- [Liberty Core — AppsUser Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/main-components/users/): The AppsUser component is a user settings dialog in Liberty Core.
- [Liberty Core — Styled Button Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/button/): The `Button` component in Liberty Core is a styled button that provides consistent theming and behavior across applications.
- [Liberty Core — Styled Card Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/card/): The `Card` component in Liberty Core provides a customizable UI container with support for elevation, transitions, and interactions.
- [Liberty Core — Styled Dialog Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/dialog/): The `Dialog` components provide structured elements for building modal dialogs with proper styling, responsiveness, and accessibility.
- [Liberty Core — Styled Div Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/div/): The `Div` component is a styled wrapper based on `styled.div` from Emotion.
- [Liberty Core — Styled Form Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/form/): The `Form` components provide styled wrappers for HTML forms, ensuring consistent spacing and layout in authentication pages and user input sections.
- [Liberty Core — Global Styles](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/global-styles/): The `GlobalStyles` component applies system-wide styles using `@emotion/react`'s `Global` API.
- [Liberty Core — Styled Icon Button Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/icon-button/): The `IconButton` components are predefined styled buttons built on top of the `IconButton` from Liberty Core.
- [Liberty Core — Icon Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/icons/): The Liberty Core Icon Set provides a predefined collection of Material Icons and Font Awesome Icons wrapped in a standardized interface for easier integration.
- [Liberty Core — Styled Input Components](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/styled-elements/input/): The `Input_White` component is a predefined styled input field that ensures consistent text and label colors across different themes.

- [Liberty Core — Table Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/tables-lists/table/): The `Table` component provides a structured way to display data in rows and columns.
- [Liberty Core — Tree Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/tables-lists/tree/): The `Tree` component is used to display hierarchical data in an expandable and collapsible format.
- [Liberty Core — Alert Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/alert/): The `Alert` component provides a styled alert message with various severity levels.
- [Liberty Core — AlertMessage Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/alert-message/): The `AlertMessage` component is a wrapper around the `Alert` component that provides automatic dismissal for non-error messages.
- [Liberty Core — Button Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/button/): The `Button` component provides a customizable button with multiple variants and props.
- [Liberty Core — Card Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/card/): The `Card` component is a versatile container that can display structured content, such as headers, actions, and clickable areas.
- [Liberty Core — Checkbox Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/checkbox/): The `Checkbox` component is a custom-styled checkbox that supports indeterminate states, labels, and various label placements.
- [Liberty Core — CircularProgress Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/circular-progress/): The `CircularProgress` component displays a rotating loader, commonly used to indicate an ongoing operation.
- [Liberty Core — Collapse Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/collapse/): The `Collapse` component allows content to expand and collapse smoothly with an animation.
- [Liberty Core — Divider Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/divider/): The `Divider` component is used to separate content with a thin line.
- [Liberty Core — FlexPanels Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/flex/): The `FlexPanels` component is a flexible, resizable layout container that allows dynamic panel resizing and optional drag-and-drop reordering.
- [Liberty Core — AdvancedFlexPanels Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/flex-advanced/): The `AdvancedFlexPanels` component is a bi-dimensional, resizable layout system that allows for: - Dynamic resizing of both rows and columns - Drag-and-drop reordering of child elements - Smooth animations for user interactions
- [Liberty Core — IconButton Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/icon-button/): The `IconButton` component is a button wrapper specifically for icons, offering: - Customizable icon size - Disabled and selected states - Hover effects with scaling animation
- [Liberty Core — LoadingIndicator Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/loading-indicator/): The `LoadingIndicator` component provides a visual loading state indicator with a customizable message and color.
- [Liberty Core — MarkDown Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/markdown/): The `MarkDown` component renders markdown content and supports syntax highlighting for code blocks, tables, and links.
- [Liberty Core — SnackMessage Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/snack-message/): The `SnackMessage` component displays temporary alert messages (snack messages) that disappear after a set duration.
- [Liberty Core — Toggle & ToggleGroup Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/toggle-button/): The `Toggle` component represents a selectable button that can be used alone or inside a `ToggleGroup` for grouped selection.
- [Liberty Core — Tooltip Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/tooltip/): The `Tooltip` component provides a simple way to display contextual hints when hovering over an element.
- [Liberty Core — Typography Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/components/ui-elements/typography/): The `Typography` component is used for consistent text styling across the application.
- [Liberty Core](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/getting-started/): Liberty Core — modular React framework with reusable UI components, context providers and application management tools for building modern apps.
- [Creating a New React App with Liberty Core](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/new-project/): Step-by-step guide to bootstrap a new React project with Liberty Core: OIDC authentication, translations and error handling included.
- [Liberty Core — Applications Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/applications/): The `Applications Configuration` defines multiple applications within the Liberty Framework.
- [Liberty Core — AppProvider Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/appprovider/): The `AppProvider` is a context provider that manages global state for the Liberty Framework.
- [Liberty Core — Authentication & Token Management](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/authentication/): The authentication system in Liberty Framework uses an access token mechanism.
- [Liberty Core — ErrorBoundary Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/error-boundary/): The `ErrorBoundary` component is a React class component that catches JavaScript errors anywhere in its child component tree.
- [Liberty Core — Modules Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/modules/): The `Modules` configuration determines which application features are enabled or disabled.
- [Liberty Core — Theme Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/themes/): The Theme Configuration in Liberty Core defines the application's primary color scheme, typography, background styles, and dark mode behavior.
- [Liberty Core — TranslationProvider Component](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/translations/): The `TranslationProvider` is a wrapper for internationalization (i18n) using i18next in the Liberty Framework.
- [Liberty Core — useMediaQuery & useDeviceDetection](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/use-media-query/): These hooks help in detecting screen sizes and device types for responsive UI design.
- [Liberty Core — Users Configuration](https://docs.nomana-it.fr/liberty/core/services/users/): The `Users Configuration` defines user profiles within the Liberty Framework.
